what_it_does: KVMSR+UDWeave enables programmers to write irregular graph algorithms that scale to millions of parallel operations on the UpDown supercomputer architecture. Graph algorithms—which traverse networks of connected nodes—are notoriously difficult to parallelize efficiently. This work cleanly separates three concerns: how much parallelism to expose, how to bind computations to logical units, and where data should be placed in the distributed memory system.
method_in_detail: The programming model leverages specific features of the UpDown supercomputer: the ability to name computation locations directly and a shared global address space that abstracts away physical memory distribution. By decoupling parallelism expression from data placement and computation binding, programmers can more intuitively express maximum parallelism while letting the runtime system optimize data locality and load balancing.
